title: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water

verses.sa: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः । नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥
verses.tr: Ever united with Me, steadfast in vows, they worship Me by chanting, striving, and bowing with devotion.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks you to listen for the first action that comes in this list of devotion. Hear how the verse begins.

body.text: Ever united with Me, steadfast in vows, they worship Me by chanting, striving, and bowing with devotion. The word kritayantah, chanting, comes second, but the first action is kritayantah, chanting. Krishna places the chanting of his name at the very start of the practice. Krishna then describes a second way these devotees worship him, through the sacrifice of knowledge.

verses.sa: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते । एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
verses.tr: Others worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing Me as one, as separate, or as the all-facing form.
verses.angle: Ananye: the others who come through knowing
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has watched Krishna teach many paths. Now Krishna names the path of understanding. Listen for how many ways he says a person can know him.

body.text: Others worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing Me as one, as separate, or as the all-facing form. The word ananye, others, tells us that Krishna is adding another kind of worshipper to the list, one who comes not with flowers but with understanding. Krishna now speaks of the all-facing form, the one who sees everything at once.

verses.sa: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् । मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥
verses.tr: I am the sacrifice, I am the ritual, I am the offering, I am the herb, I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering. I am the sacred syllable Om, the Vedas, the father, mother, supporter, grandfather, object of knowledge, purifier, and imperishable seed of this world.
verses.angle: Krishna is the ritual and the offering
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Last time Krishna said people worship him in many ways, and now he names every part of the sacred fire ritual.

body.text: I am the sacrifice, I am the ritual, I am the offering, I am the herb, I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering. I am the sacred syllable Om, the Vedas, the father, mother, supporter, grandfather, object of knowledge, purifier, and imperishable seed of this world. Krishna says he is the fire, the ghee, the herb, and the act of offering, so the worshipper, the worship, and the object of worship are all one. He continues to say he is the father, the mother, and the grandfather of this world.

verses.sa: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
verses.tr: I am the father of this world, the mother, the supporter, and the grandfather. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
verses.angle: Father, mother, and the three Vedas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The Gita has been listing what Krishna is. Now he moves from the ritual to the source. What is the answer to the question of where everything comes from?

body.text: I am the father of this world, the mother, the supporter, and the grandfather. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas. Listen to how the verse moves from family to scripture: father, mother, grandfather, and then the Rig, Sama, and Yajur. He is not only the world’s ancestor but also the knowledge that gives it order. Krishna then continues to name himself as the goal, the shelter, and the final resting place of all things.

verses.sa: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the refuge, the friend, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed.
verses.angle: Eleven roles that Krishna claims as his own
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now lists eleven roles he fills, from the start of creation to its end. Listen to how he names himself as the goal, the shelter, and the seed.

body.text: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the refuge, the friend, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed. Krishna lists eleven roles and claims them all. He is the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the dwelling, the refuge, the well-wisher, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed. Krishna then says he heats the world as the sun, holds back the rain, and is both immortality and death.

verses.sa: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च । अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥
verses.tr: I heat the world as the sun, I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Amritam and Mrityuh: one reality holds both
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to feel two forces in the world that shape everything, and to hear how they are named.

body.text: I heat the world as the sun, I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna. The words amritam, immortality, and mrityuh, death, sit side by side. This is not a choice between them, but one reality holding both the welcome and the feared side of life. Krishna then turns to those who seek heaven through sacrifice, and to what they truly find there.

verses.sa: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापायज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते । ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकमश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥
verses.tr: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna about the limits of ritual. He describes a group of people who perform sacrifices and ask for a specific reward. Listen to what they seek.

body.text: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings. Listen to the reward they ask for, heaven, and the pleasures they enjoy there. They reach the realm of the radiant beings, but their enjoyment is only the result of accumulated merit. Once their merit runs out, they fall back to the mortal world, caught in repeated coming and going.

verses.sa: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालंक्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति । एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्नागतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥
verses.tr: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going.
verses.angle: merit runs out and the soul returns to earth
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the heaven-world as a vast reward that ends. Listen for the moment when the soul must return to the mortal world.

body.text: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going. Heaven bought with merit runs out, Krishna says, and the buyer comes back down to earth. He then turns to those who fix their minds on him alone, offering a different kind of security.

verses.sa: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verses.tr: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus, I carry their welfare and security.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just exposed the limits of the ritual path. Now he makes a direct promise to those who turn to him with undivided attention.

body.text: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus, I carry their welfare and security. The word ananyah means with no other focus, and Krishna promises to personally carry the welfare and security of those who keep their mind on him alone. He then addresses those who worship other radiant beings and says they still end up worshipping him, but in the wrong way.

verses.sa: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
verses.tr: Even those who, filled with trust, worship other radiant beings, worship Me alone, but in the wrong way, O son of Kunti.
verses.angle: Mamam eva: they worship Me alone
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns to those who worship other radiant beings, showing that their trust still reaches him.

body.text: Even those who, filled with trust, worship other radiant beings, worship Me alone, but in the wrong way, O son of Kunti. The word mamam eva, Me alone, appears in the second half. Krishna says that even those who worship other gods are in fact worshipping him alone, though they do not know the true way. Yet the next verse warns that because they do not know him in truth, their worship ultimately falls away.

verses.sa: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च । न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥
verses.tr: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away.
verses.angle: abhijananti, they know, the hinge of the verse
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna says he is the one who receives every sacrifice. Listen to the word that captures what happens when people miss that truth.

body.text: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away. The hinge of the verse is the word abhijananti, they know. Krishna says that because people do not know him in truth, they fall away. Krishna then states that those who worship other beings reach those beings, but those devoted to him come to him.

verses.sa: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः । भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥
verses.tr: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me.
verses.angle: Mamam: the destination for those devoted only to Krishna
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said he is the true lord of all worship, and that people who do not know him fall away. Now he explains where different kinds of worship lead.

body.text: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me. Listen to the word mamam, me, at the end of the verse. It is the destination for those whose devotion is aimed only at me, while other devotions reach other ends. Krishna then says he accepts even a simple leaf, flower, fruit, or water, if offered with devotion.

verses.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
verses.tr: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept that devoted offering from the pure-hearted.
verses.angle: Krishna consumes even a leaf or water
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues to describe the relationship that can hold a life together, now turning to the smallest gifts a person can offer.

body.text: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept that devoted offering from the pure-hearted. The word I accept is a form of the verb to eat, and Krishna says he consumes whatever a pure-hearted person offers, from a leaf to water. Krishna then tells Arjuna to dedicate every action, meal, and gift to him.

next.title: Whatever you do, offer it to Me
